record.notes: SIGNUP PATH, read. The account is created at https://signup.oraclecloud.com/ and nowhere else; oracle.com/cloud/free is the marketing page and signup.cloud.oracle.com serves the same shell. The page is a React application whose HTML carries no form, so the field list is taken from Oracle's own signup document, which walks the same form step by step. In order: country (some countries, Russia named, need the Terms accepted by checkbox), name, email, CAPTCHA, an email verification link valid 30 minutes, a password of 8-40 characters with upper, lower, digit and symbol, an optional company, a cloud account name, a home region that cannot be changed afterwards, the Terms, then address and phone number, then the card, then 'Start my free trial'. There is no identity document and no company requirement; the company field is explicitly optional. The home region matters more than the card: a user in a country with no Oracle region must pick an adjacent one, and the region cannot be changed, so a wrong pick is a new account. THE GRANT IS TWO PRODUCTS, not one. Always Free is the unlimited-period allowance described in free_tier.stated. The USD 300 is a separate 30-day trial that begins at the same signup and expires on its own; the FAQ says Always Free resources survive that expiry, but anything created with trial credit is reclaimed. So 'USD 300 for 90 days' is not what Oracle sells here: it is USD 300 for 30 days plus a permanent allowance. THE HOLD IS USD 1.00, published by Oracle's billing documentation, not by the signup page; the signup page says only 'a small, temporary charge' and names no amount. THE FAILURE MODE is the reason this row is a caveat and not a yes. Oracle refuses signups with a message that names three causes and no remedy, and two 2026 threads on Oracle's own forum show it arriving from Saudi Arabia and from a card that had just verified successfully. The country page says the tier is available wherever commercial OCI runs; there is no OCI region in Viet Nam, Thailand, Indonesia or the Philippines, so a registrant in one of those picks an adjacent region, and Oracle's fraud checks read the mismatch between the declared address and the connection. That is reported, not documented: nobody publishes the rule. Not established: whether a signup from any particular country succeeds, because only a signup can show it; and the true minimum boot volume, because the page states 47 GB and 50 GB in two paragraphs.

free_tier.stated: A refutation. A widely syndicated claim states that OCI Always Free includes '1 NVIDIA A10 GPU, 24GB VRAM... capped at 500 GPU-hours per month', worth about USD 640 a month, attributed to a December 2025 Oracle blog post. The official Always Free page lists no GPU at all. Its Compute section names exactly two shapes: 'up to two Always Free VM instances using the VM.Standard.E2.1.Micro shape' and 'the first 1,500 OCPU hours and 9,000 GB hours per month for free for VM instances using the VM.Standard.A1.Flex shape'. The cited blog URL returns HTTP 403 and has no Wayback capture.
free_tier.notes: pay-as-you-go list prices per GPU-hour from the vendor's price list data: H100 USD 10, A100 80 GB (A100 v2) USD 4, L40S USD 3.5; no RTX 4090 and no L4 row. unverified: the price list states no billing granularity and no minimum bill for GPU shapes.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: Nothing to chain: the entitlement does not exist on the page that would define it.

record.notes: The secondary article also contains arithmetic errors that a reader can check: it prices the A10 at USD 1.28 an hour in one sentence and says that maps to VM.GPU3.1, which is a V100 shape, and it describes BM.GPU.A10.1, which is not a shape name on OCI's price list (the bare metal A10 shape is BM.GPU.A10.4). Oracle did announce an Always Free compute reduction enforced from 18 August 2026, cutting Ampere A1 from 4 OCPU and 24 GB to 2 OCPU and 12 GB, and the official page reflects the reduced figures, which is independent evidence that the page read is current. The one recorded is the better-evidenced. The claim that OCI Always Free includes an A10 GPU has no page behind it, and that claim is dead. The provider is not: it sells preemptible GPU capacity at about half the on-demand rate, with a two-minute termination event and VM.GPU2 and VM.GPU3 as supported preemptible shapes, as this record's own evidence rows state. `dead` was read as 'OCI has nothing', which the evidence contradicts.

The Always Free Object Storage allowance is '20 GB of combined Standard tier, Infrequent Access tier, and Archive tier data' per tenancy. Quotas: 500 repos total and 500 images per repo PER region.

egress.terms: Free up to 10 TB per month on every tenancy. Terms state: 'Public internet egress | 10 TB/month free. Oracle charges significantly less for data egress over the public internet in all global regions. Customers are not charged for the first 10 TB of data egress per month.'

record.tooling: docker/skopeo/ORAS. Auth via IAM auth token ('create an Auth Token via your user settings and login with the Docker CLI').
record.chaining: The 20 GB Always Free OSS is small, but egress is 10 TB/month per tenancy and repos can be made public so pulls need no auth: 'if a user has the complete path to the image, they can pull it, with no authentication needed.' Multiple Always Free tenancies are limited. 'One Oracle Cloud Free Trial or Always Free account is permitted per person'. So this scales by tenancy policy, not by unlimited accounts.
record.limits_note: 500 repos/region, 500 images/repo; public repos pullable anonymously if the path is known; auto-cleanup retention policies available; storage beyond 20 GB Always Free is billed at Object Storage Standard rates.
record.reliability_note: Public pull works but the console is hidden from anonymous users; the binding constraint is the 20 GB storage allowance and the one-tenancy-per-person rule, not throughput.
